sections.html:
Two offices split Lake County's property tax work. The Property Appraiser decides what each parcel is worth and handles exemptions. The Tax Collector prints the bill and takes the payment. When something looks wrong, call the office that owns that part, because neither one can fix the other's mistakes.

Changes to a name, mailing address, parcel location or assessed value on the roll go through the appraiser at (352) 253-2150. Collection starts November 1, and a notice that never shows up is still the owner's problem to pay. If a lender escrows your taxes, the notice carries a code at the top and a banner at the bottom.

  • Property Appraiser: values every parcel, takes homestead and other exemption filings, and mails the August notice of proposed taxes.
  • Tax Collector: prints and mails the bill, accepts payment, and runs the June tax certificate sale on unpaid accounts.
  • Clerk of the Circuit Court: files the deed, collects the deed stamps, and supports the value adjustment board.

Pay in November and Lake County takes up to 4 percent off the bill. The discount drops a point each month through February, and the window closes at the end of March.

Lake County payment schedule for the full annual bill
Paid in full byDiscount
November 304 percent
December 313 percent
January 312 percent
February 281 percent
March 31Gross amount, no discount

A mailed payment earns the discount based on its postmark. On April 1 a 3 percent statutory interest charge is added to the total due, and tax certificates go up for sale on unpaid items by June 1.

Installment plans and the certificate sale schedule are set by the collector each year, so call that office before you count on either.

sections.h2: What millage rates apply to a Lake County home?
sections.html:
It depends on where the house sits. The Property Appraiser's 2026 final millage rate sheet gives a separate total for every taxing district code, and the totals run from the low 13s in unincorporated areas to the high 19s in some cities.

The unincorporated codes at the top of the sheet total 13.0632, 13.0670 or 13.4678, depending on the code. Three lines repeat in every row: the county general fund at 5.0254, the school board state line at 3.0560 and the school board local line at 2.9980. What separates one district from another is the extra layers, such as a city levy, a fire or ambulance district, a hospital district or a community development district.

  • Clermont: 16.2875 total, with a city line of 4.2000.
  • Leesburg: 15.8704 total, with a city line of 3.3783.
  • Mount Dora: 18.7921 total, with a city line of 6.3000.
  • Eustis: 19.8819 total, with a city line of 7.3898.
  • Montverde: 15.3975 total, with a city line of 2.8300.

Find your own code on the tax notice or the appraiser's parcel record, then read that row of the sheet. The cities on the sheet are Astatula, Clermont, Eustis, Fruitland Park, Groveland, Howey-in-the-Hills, Lady Lake, Leesburg, Mascotte, Minneola, Montverde, Mount Dora, Tavares and Umatilla.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption and Save Our Homes
sections.html:
An owner who lives in the house on January 1 and files by March 1 can exempt up to $50,000 of value. School levies reach only the first slice of that exemption, so the school lines on the millage sheet (3.0560 and 2.9980) get the smaller break.

File Form DR-501 with the property appraiser. Renting the home or moving out ends the exemption. The appraiser's home page links a list of exemptions and how to qualify, which is where to look for senior, veteran and disability benefits that local rules may add.

Save Our Homes holds the yearly growth of a homestead's assessed value under an inflation-linked ceiling. The state chart shows 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024. A sale returns the parcel to market value, so the buyer's first full bill can look very different from yours. A seller who is moving within Florida may be able to carry the built-up cushion to the next homestead through portability, which has its own form and a three-year clock.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax when you sell the house?
sections.html:
At closing the seller and buyer split the current year's tax, and any back tax has to be cleared before title passes. The title company normally pays the collector out of the seller's share.

A house that sells in spring or summer usually has no current bill yet, because statements arrive in the fall, so the title agent works from an estimate. Get the exact figure and any older balance from the collector while the contract is still being negotiated.

  • Pull the parcel record from the appraiser and confirm the owner name and mailing address.
  • Ask the collector whether any year is delinquent or sits under a certificate.
  • Tell the title company if you have a homestead exemption so the proration uses the right figure.
  • Ask for a draft settlement statement and compare its tax line with the collector's numbers.
  • Expect the buyer's next bill to run higher, since the value resets after closing.

Deed stamps are set by statute at 70 cents per $100 of consideration. Each party stays liable even when the contract assigns the cost to one side.

Delinquency starts April 1, and a parcel left unpaid can eventually reach a tax deed sale. It first sits under a tax certificate, and the investor who holds the certificate cannot ask for a deed until two years have run.

The certificate sale opens on or before June 1. Bidders compete by accepting the lowest interest rate, and certificates nobody wants go to the county. A homestead parcel with less than $250 delinquent is issued to the county rather than auctioned. If a deed sale follows, the clerk runs a public auction and the winning bidder has to put down a nonrefundable deposit.

An owner who cannot pay can look at the homestead tax deferral. Low-income homestead owners can ask the collector to defer part of the bill on Form DR-570, filed by the end of March. A separate installment prepayment request has a May 1 date.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Lake County value?
sections.html:
If the August notice shows a value that looks off, a petition to the value adjustment board has to be filed within 25 days of that notice. Count from the date on the notice, not the day it reached your mailbox.

A denied exemption or deferral runs on its own 30-day clock, counted from the mailing date of the denial letter. The board is staffed through the Lake County clerk's office, which has its own forms page. Talk to the appraiser first, since many questions about square footage or exemption status get settled before any petition is needed.

Before you call, gather the notice, recent nearby sales, photos and any repair estimates. Those are the papers the appraiser will want to see.

Taxing authorities hold budget hearings in September and October and set final millage afterward. Those hearings are the place to speak up about rates, as opposed to the value of your own house.

faqs.q: When are Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The discount runs from 4 percent in November down to 1 percent in February, and the gross bill is due by the end of March. From April 1 a 3 percent charge attaches.

faqs.q: Who do I call to change my Lake County mailing address on a tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Lake County Property Appraiser at (352) 253-2150, not the tax collector. Name, address, location and assessed value changes all go through the appraiser.

faqs.q: What is the total millage in unincorporated Lake County?
faqs.a: The 2026 final millage sheet shows 13.0632, 13.0670 or 13.4678 for unincorporated codes, depending on the district. Your notice shows your code, and the sheet breaks out each line.

faqs.q: Does selling my Lake County house reset my tax value?
faqs.a: Yes, for the buyer. A sale counts as a change of ownership, so your capped value does not follow the house.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lake County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance, plus any certificate redemption, comes out of your proceeds at closing. Get a payoff figure from the collector's office and give it to the closing agent early.
